title: The half-finished write, repaired by a read
request:
Replica 0 alone holds (ts 5, 42) — a writer died mid-write — then someone reads

./your_program.sh abd
init 3
poke 0 5 1 42
read
state
note: The read did not just observe the register, it repaired it. Before the read, 42 existed on one replica out of three and could still have been lost; afterwards it is on a majority and cannot be. This is why the second phase is not an optimisation.

title: The same story with the second phase removed
request:
Write-back disabled, then the replica holding the value goes away

./your_program.sh abd
init 3
writeback off
poke 0 5 1 42
read
down 0
read
note: Two reads, no write between them, and the value went backwards. Nothing failed that a majority-based system is not allowed to survive — one replica of three. The history is simply not linearizable, and the missing write-back is the whole reason.
